fields.name: circular_statistics
fields.documentation: Vector-space summary of the RAW (unfitted) direction curve (v1 `vector`).

fields.name: circular_variance
fields.documentation: Circular variance in orientation space; related to selectivity and tuning width.

fields.name: hotelling_t2_p
fields.documentation: p-value of Hotelling's T-squared test of whether the orientation vectors differ from [0,0] (v1 `hotelling2test`).

fields.name: direction_hotelling_t2_p
fields.documentation: p-value of Hotelling's T-squared test on the direction vectors (v1 `direction_hotelling2test`).

fields.name: direction_dot_product_p
fields.documentation: p-value of the direction dot-product test, which uses both orientation and direction vectors to assess direction selectivity (Mazurek et al.; v1 `dot_direction_significance`).

fields.name: orientation_preference
fields.documentation: Orientation with the highest response in orientation vector space. In degrees, fixed (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [calculator units]).

fields.name: direction_preference
fields.documentation: Direction with the highest response in direction vector space. In degrees, fixed (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [calculator units]).

fields.name: interpolated_values
fields.documentation: Fit-less half-height summaries of the direction curve (v1 `vector.half_low`, `half_high`, `fwhh`, `bandwidth`, written by NDIcalc-vis-matlab +vis/+oridir/+index/oridir_vectorindexes.m). The same names as the spatial- and temporal-frequency tuning calculations' interpolated values. Jess Haley 2026-11-09 [oridir half-height values], did_v2_tuning_model_plan.md.

fields.name: half_maximum_below
fields.documentation: Walking from the peak toward lower directions, wrapping around the circle, the first direction where the mean response falls to half its maximum, in degrees, in [0, 360) (v1 `vector.half_low`). NaN when the calculator found no such point (T14: attempted, not obtained; the reason is in `notes`).

fields.name: half_maximum_above
fields.documentation: The same, walking toward higher directions (v1 `vector.half_high`). NaN when the calculator found no such point (T14: attempted, not obtained; the reason is in `notes`).

fields.name: full_width_half_height
fields.documentation: The angular distance from half_maximum_below up to half_maximum_above across the peak, in degrees (v1 `vector.fwhh`; on a circle it is not their plain difference). NaN where the writer wrote Inf (either point not found); the reason is in `notes` and the v1 round trip writes Inf back.

fields.name: bandwidth
fields.documentation: log2(half_maximum_above / half_maximum_below), in octaves, as the calculator reports it (v1 `vector.bandwidth`). NaN where the writer wrote Inf (a point not found, or half_maximum_below exactly 0 degrees); the reason is in `notes` and the v1 round trip writes Inf back. An octave bandwidth of a direction depends on where 0 degrees sits.
